last_result.content:
## 4 Retention and Deletion

The vendor must delete or return all employee data within 60 days after expiration or
termination and must certify the deletion in writing. Backup and archival copies must be
covered, with a defined purge cycle if immediate deletion is impracticable. Retention beyond
the 60-day window is acceptable only under a specific legal hold or an identified legal
requirement, only for the period that requirement runs, and only under the continuing
security and confidentiality obligations of the agreement. Open-ended retention for
unspecified legal purposes, or retention governed solely by the vendor's own schedule, is
not acceptable.

last_result.content:
## 4.1 Retention and Post-Termination Handling

Provider will retain Employee Data during the Subscription Term and thereafter for so long as
Provider determines retention is necessary or appropriate for legal, regulatory, audit, or
dispute-resolution purposes. Following expiration or termination, Provider will make Employee
Data available for Customer export for thirty (30) days, after which Provider will delete
Employee Data in accordance with Provider's standard retention schedule then in effect.
Provider has no obligation to certify deletion or to delete Employee Data held in backup,
archival, log, or aggregated form.

action.title: Inconsistent Data Retention Policy
action.analysis: The Playbook mandates that all employee data must be deleted within 60 days after expiration or termination, with a certification of deletion required. However, the Data Handling Exhibit allows for indefinite retention based on Provider's discretion for unspecified legal, regulatory, audit, or dispute-resolution purposes, and does not require deletion of data held in backup, archival, log, or aggregated form. This conflicts with the Playbook's strict requirements.
action.recommendation: Propose redlining the Data Handling Exhibit to align with the Playbook's stringent data retention and deletion policies.

quotes.text: The vendor must delete or return all employee data within 60 days after expiration or termination and must certify the deletion in writing. Backup and archival copies must be covered, with a defined purge cycle if immediate deletion is impracticable. Retention beyond the 60-day window is acceptable only under a specific legal hold or an identified legal requirement, only for the period that requirement runs, and only under the continuing security and confidentiality obligations of the agreement.

Provider will retain Employee Data during the Subscription Term and thereafter for so long as Provider determines retention is necessary or appropriate for legal, regulatory, audit, or dispute-resolution purposes. Following expiration or termination, Provider will make Employee Data available for Customer export for thirty (30) days, after which Provider will delete Employee Data in accordance with Provider's standard retention schedule then in effect. Provider has no obligation to certify deletion or to delete Employee Data held in backup, archival, log, or aggregated form.
